message_source_quote: Prior white-bear steering (ref-05) contrasts *think* vs *don't-think* within matched pairs (same concept/sentence). This submission contrasts *think* against the *preference* suppression paradigm
writeup_source_quote: Prior white-bear steering contrasts *think* against *don't-think* within matched pairs (same concept, same sentence). I instead contrast *think* against the *preference* suppression paradigm

differences.what: message reports additional confirmatory experiments relating the method to the source (that white-bear's own think/don't-think direction also works at ~0.78, and that content-based/function-vector contrasts fail, matching the paper's negative findings) — none of this overlap-verification work is mentioned in the write-up
differences.message_quote: I confirmed along the way that white-bear's own think/don't-think direction works (also ~0.78), that content-based and function-vector-style contrasts do *not* work (matching the paper's negative findings), and that the think-vs-preference contrast transfers to the association family with no association-specific signal.

rationale: Both documents credit white-bear/Raman 2026 steering as the direct basis for the method and make the identical novelty claim: contrasting think-vs-preference-suppression instead of think-vs-don't-think, on a different item set, concepts and carriers. The message additionally reports extra validation work (reproducing the baseline white-bear direction's performance and ruling out content/function-vector contrasts in line with the source paper's own negative findings) that is not mentioned anywhere in the write-up, making the message materially richer on this one point while the core source/novelty framing is otherwise equal.
